html:
Lê Lợi was a landowner from Lam Sơn in Thanh Hóa, Vietnam, who led a ten-year war against the Ming occupation and founded the Later Lê dynasty in 1428. He was born in 1385.

The Ming had invaded in 1407 and tried to make Vietnam a Chinese province, carrying off books and craftsmen. Lê Lợi rose in 1418 with a small band and fought a long guerrilla war in the hills. In 1427 his forces destroyed a Ming relief army at Chi Lăng, and the Ming withdrew. Nguyễn Trãi, his adviser, wrote the victory proclamation that Vietnamese still learn in school.

Legend says Lê Lợi received a magic sword from a golden turtle and returned it in a lake in Hanoi, since called Hoàn Kiếm, the lake of the returned sword. His dynasty ruled, at least in name, until 1789, and under Lê Thánh Tông it issued the Hồng Đức Code and conquered Champa.
